title: gfx938 declares operation kind mma and two dot contracts that no Corpus case exercises, so the Gate says nothing about the declaration
executor_revision: none: this record is read from the Corpus and the Target document

evidence.retained: the Corpus at the commit named above; no campaign is involved
sites: compiler/targets/gfx938.json -- declares mma, triton.dot.fp16_fp32 and triton.dot.fp8e4m3_fp32, with its BW1101 disassembly and oracle citations
corpus/schedules/ -- gfx938 has three cases and every one is load, elementwise, reduce and store; none contains an mma operation
src/open_cake_ir/compiler/corpus.py -- check_corpus closes each case to case_id, schedule and expected
tests/contracts/test_gfx938.py::Gfx938DeclaredContracts -- reads the declaration, which is not the same as exercising it

observation:
The Corpus Gate passes 151 of 151 with the declaration present and with it absent, because no case reaches it. The tests added with F-2026-09-17-008 read the Target document and the two analysis tables; none compiles an mma Schedule for this target. So the declaration's hardware evidence is real and its lowering path is real, and nothing in the repository's own gates would notice if either stopped being true.

This is the sibling of F-2026-09-17-004 rather than a repeat of it. That record is about gfx1151 declaring `cast` with no demonstration at all; here the demonstration exists and was measured on a BW1101 -- disassembly showing v_mmac_f32_16x16x16_f16 and v_mmac_f32_16x16x32_fp8_fp8, and an elementwise comparison against a torch oracle at 64x64x64 -- but it lives in a citation and in a session transcript, not in a case the Gate replays. The two share what makes them worth writing down: a Target document can state a fact that no gate is obliged to re-check.

Recorded as its own id at an independent reviewer's request. The gap was written into F-2026-09-17-008's prose and onto its index line, and that record is closed; an open gap inside a closed finding is not tracked by anything that reads the index.

Closed by authoring both halves. The second is the point: the drift case is the input two independent reviewers each had to construct by hand to show the dtype gate had stopped running, and the Gate replays it now instead of anyone remembering to. Adopting the two expectations was a separate act through tools/refresh_corpus_expectations.py --write, and the preview it prints first listed exactly the two new ids and no existing case, which is what distinguishes adopting a new pin from re-pinning one that drifted.

The class recurred inside the change that closed this record, which is worth recording here rather than as a new id. Three more contracts were declared on this target afterwards -- ocml.tanh.f32, triton.dot.fp32_ieee and triton.dot.fp32_tf32 -- plus triton.dot.fp8e4m3_fp32 from the original pair. An independent reviewer measured which of them the Gate actually reaches by deleting each from the Target document and re-running check_corpus: triton.dot.fp32_tf32 and triton.dot.fp8e4m3_fp32 could both be removed with the Gate still passing 156 of 156. Two declarations carrying device citations that no case exercised.

Both now have cases, and all five fail the Gate when removed. The standing guard is tests/contracts/test_gfx938.py::test_every_declared_contract_is_reached_by_a_corpus_case, which matches the Target's declared set against the contracts named in the manifest's gfx938 schedules -- cheaper than the deletion sweep and catching the same thing.

Run across every target rather than this one, the deletion sweep finds eleven declarations elsewhere still Gate-inert: sm_103a's triton.dot.fp32_ieee, triton.dot.fp32_tf32, triton.dot.fp8e4m3_block_scale_fp32, triton.atomic_add.i32.relaxed.gpu, libdevice.tanh.f32 and ptx.fma.rn.f32; metal.fma.f32 and metal.precise.tanh.f32 on apple_gpu_family7 and _9; and metal.precise.tanh.f32 alone on apple_gpu_family8. sm_100a has none.

An earlier version of this paragraph said nine, named sm_100a's atomic among them and gave both Metal contracts for all three Apple targets. That was not the sweep's result: it came from a cheaper derivation that scanned named contracts in JSON schedules, which misses the Python schedules under examples/ -- metal_fma.py is the only case reaching apple_gpu_family8's fma -- and misses contracts an operation binds without naming, which is why sm_100a's atomic looked unreached. The figure was attributed to a measurement that contradicts it, and its own enumeration summed to thirteen rather than nine. Those predate this record and are not gfx938's, but they are the same defect, and a test named for a general invariant while examining one target would have repeated the omission the invariant is about. The count per target is pinned by tests/contracts/test_instruction_contracts.py::DeclaredContractsTheGateCannotSpeakFor, whose derivation now reads Python schedules and implicit bindings and reproduces the sweep's eleven exactly, with each of the two misses pinned as its own test.
proposed_change:
Author one gfx938 mma Corpus case and adopt its expectation as a separate reviewed act (tools/refresh_corpus_expectations.py --write), with the new case as the stated reason -- never as a regeneration that makes a failing gate pass. The case should use the declared fp16 contract at the shape the citation measured, so the Gate replays the same thing the evidence claims. Until then the declaration is evidence-gated but not gate-covered, and this record is what says so.

Done. One adaptation worth recording: the sm_100a schedule this was derived from declares a per-thread register budget, and Triton's HIPOptions carries no field to apply one, so a gfx938 case carrying it would declare a cap that is dropped rather than enforced -- TRITON_AMDGCN_REGISTER_BUDGET_UNENFORCEABLE, which also blocks lowering and would have left the case never reaching emission. The budget is omitted, as the gfx938 rmsnorm case omits it, so the accepted case lowers and the Gate pins its emitted source.
verified_by: the Corpus Gate at the successor: 153 of 153 matched, with gfx938-gemm-bias-mma-accepted lowering to tl.dot over fp16 operands into an fp32 accumulator, and gfx938-gemm-bias-mma-operand-dtype-drift refused by two blocking MMA_OPERAND_DTYPE_DIFFERS; extended after the class recurred: all five gfx938 contracts now fail the Gate when removed from the Target document, measured by deletion, and the invariant is pinned by a standing test rather than by a sweep somebody has to remember to run
